facts.text: Lucia premiered on 26 September 1835 at the Teatro di San Carlo in Naples.
facts.evidence: The opera premiered on 26 September 1835 at the Teatro di San Carlo in Naples.

facts.text: The libretto is loosely based on Walter Scott’s 1819 novel The Bride of Lammermoor, written when Scotland’s history and folklore were all the rage.
evidence: loosely based upon Walter Scott's 1819 historical novel The Bride of Lammermoor
there was also a widespread interest in the history and culture of Scotland

facts.text: With Rossini retired and Bellini recently dead, Donizetti was left as “the sole reigning genius of Italian opera”.
evidence: Vincenzo Bellini had died shortly before the premiere of Lucia leaving Donizetti as "the sole reigning genius of Italian opera"

facts.text: Lucia was never absent from the Met’s repertory for more than one season at a time from 1903 until 1972.
facts.evidence: The opera was never absent from the repertory of the Metropolitan Opera for more than one season at a time from 1903 until 1972.

facts.text: After World War II, Maria Callas and Joan Sutherland gave the opera new life.
facts.evidence: a number of sopranos were instrumental in giving new life to the opera, including Maria Callas

facts.text: Donizetti scored the mad scene for glass harmonica and soprano. A flute is more commonly used, mostly for practical reasons.
